precepts.text: The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker. For pride is the beginning of sin: it is the beginning of you falling to your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite; because you knew better, you had all the warning signs, you were given a way out as we read in 1 Corinthians 10, but pride overcame you and your mind was not on the Lord when your back was against the wall. And he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities. When that pride overtakes you, the Lord adds to your demise and leaves you to Satan, because your mind is not right.
precepts.point: Pride. Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. You think you know it all, you think you have all the wisdom and understanding; but pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction. You do not want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction”. Where does pride begin? Sirach: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: the beginning of you falling to sin, falling for your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite. You knew better. You had all the warning signs, all the opportunity, everything placed in front of you. You were given a way out, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 said: God will with the temptation make a way to escape. But pride overcame you. Your mind wasn't on the Lord when your back was against the wall.

“and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”. When you have that pride, a negro is unstoppable; a prideful negro, oh my God. “and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds things to your demise: I'm going to leave you to Satan to gobble you on up, because your mind ain't right; you're too prideful.

That is why pride goes before destruction. Pride removes correction; you don't want to hear it. You think you know it all, you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride isolates you, and it precedes the collapse.

precepts.text: For froward thoughts separate from God. Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible. When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him; you cannot be both.
precepts.point: Pride. Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. You think you know it all, you think you have all the wisdom and understanding; but pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction. You do not want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Sirach says pride begins when one departs from God. The Wisdom of Solomon shows how a man departs: “For froward thoughts separate from God”.

Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible. Period. That's what it is.

When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him. You can't be both. So pride starts in the thoughts: the moment your thinking goes outside of the scriptures, you have separated yourself from God, and a haughty spirit is on its way to the fall. That is why the man who meditates on the scriptures has something to pull from when temptation comes, and the froward man doesn't.

precepts.text: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together. Why is that last one beautiful? Because it is hard for two different personalities to come together and be on one accord. Marriage takes time, brothers and sisters; it takes years and experience. But three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth. A poor man that is proud has no humility whatsoever: nobody can tell him anything, he has all the answers and no fruits in his life. That is how much the Lord hates pride.
precepts.point: Pride. Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. You think you know it all, you think you have all the wisdom and understanding; but pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction. You do not want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
This is how much the Lord hates pride. Sirach first shows what God loves: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren the Lord loves; the love of neighbors the Lord loves. And a man and wife that agree together: why is that beautiful? Because it's hard for two different personalities to come together and be on the same accord. That's why marriage takes time, brothers and sisters. It isn't overnight; it takes years and experience.

Now the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.” He is offended at their life. A negro that's poor and proud: I hate that negro, I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. How can you be that way?

It means you have no humility whatsoever. Nobody can tell you anything; you have all the answers, but no fruits in your life, no solutions, no shame. That is the pride that goes before destruction, and God's soul hates it.

precepts.text: When a man's ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him. That's what happened with Joseph.
precepts.point: But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison. The keeper committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners; whatever Joseph did, the Lord made it to prosper.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Even in prison, “the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.” The keeper “committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison,” and “looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.”

Solomon gives the reason: “When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” That is what happened with Joseph. He was a Hebrew slave, accused of attacking his master's wife, locked in the place where the king's prisoners were bound, and his very jailer became favourable to him and handed him the whole prison.

It is the same pattern all through Joseph's life: in Potiphar's house the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house “for Joseph’s sake,” just as Laban was blessed for Jacob's sake when Jacob worked for him. Joseph's ways pleased the Lord; he refused sin even when it cost him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it to prosper. Keep your ways pleasing to God, and he will make even those set over you in captivity to be at peace with you.

precepts.text: An ungodly man diggeth up evil: and in his lips there is as a burning fire. That is the bitter brother always digging up the old things.
precepts.point: They hold grudges, as we read in Leviticus 19; they revisit past wrongs; they lack forgiveness, as Ecclesiasticus 28 showed; and there is the quiet resentment, sitting back stewing in silence.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
The first sign of a bitter brother is that he is easily offended; he will “make a man an offender for a word”. The next sign is that he holds grudges, the thing Leviticus 19:18 forbids: “Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people”. And he is always revisiting past wrongs.

Proverbs names him: “An ungodly man diggeth up evil”. That is the bitter brother digging up evil, the plumber brother, digging up old ish. As we say up in the States, he's digging it up like he's a plumber.

“and in his lips there is as a burning fire.” That is deceit, and he is always hating. That is the brother with the banana on his lips, the certified hater like Cain: I don't like that. That's you.

So the one who makes a man an offender for a word is the same one who keeps digging up the old things. He lacks forgiveness, as Sirach 28 showed, and he will not let the past rest. Brother, you are not in the right spirit.

precepts.text: The preparations of the heart in man and the answer of the tongue are from the Lord: even your coming to the leadership table you want to fight was ordained before time, and the Lord seals a man's instruction in his sleep.
precepts.point: Your issue is not with leadership; you are bitter towards the Lord.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
Christ told the twelve, “Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven”. Someone thinks it's just leadership saying it. No: “The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord.” The Lord had already ordained you to come up to that leadership table. Even your walking up to the council you want to go against was declared before time, as Isaiah 46:10 says, declaring the end from the beginning. God already agreed.

The preparing of your mind is from the Lord. You may say, I'm going to get up at 9:00 today and make it to the gym. The Lord says no, you are getting up at 10:00, and you'll get out the bed on the left-hand side and stub your damn toe. You set that timer to the T all week, you're a light sleeper, and that joker doesn't ring, because that was the Lord's doing. The Lord seals man's instruction in his sleep.

And the answer of the tongue, is that from the man or the woman? It is from the Lord. The Lord dictates even what you are going to respond back. The Lord may send a spirit down on you to go contrary to the doctrine, contrary to what leadership says in counsel to save your life, and you don't even catch that it is a spirit speaking through you. That is also a learning experience, for you to catch yourself.

But many cannot shake that legion. They ride that wave onto the bitterness boat and find themselves outside the congregation, making three- and four-part emotional videos and complaining on Clubhouse about how they were done unjustly. Then the Lord blinds your mind; you are reprobate, and only if the Lord chooses will he bring you back.

So your issue is not with leadership; you are bitter toward the Lord. Leadership has nothing to gain by telling you the word. All we gave you was the word of God, and we will be judged for it. Take it here and forbear, or go out there and get burnt. Our people hate their freedom; they are fearful of freedom, of responsibility, and of leadership.

precepts.text: I am the true vine, the root and offspring of David, Revelation 22:16, and my Father is the husbandman; ye are God's husbandry, 1 Corinthians 3:9. Every branch that beareth not fruit he taketh away, because one bad apple spoils the bunch and hinders growth; every branch that beareth fruit he purgeth that it may bring forth more. Abide in me, for the branch cannot bear fruit of itself.
precepts.point: The fear is not the fear of the servant who hid his talent or the brother making excuses because he is nervous; Psalms 119:120, my flesh trembleth for fear of thee and I am afraid of thy judgments. He is the King of terrors.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.” Going into Passover season, which is also purging season, we refocus and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. Christ shows how the purging is done: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.”

A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground, and Christ is that root: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” And the Father is the husbandman because we are what he planted: “ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.” We are his plants, his trees, which in that day become the trees of righteousness.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away.” That is why we cannot be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. If we do not bring forth fruit, he takes away our candlestick: you did not do what I created you to do, so you cannot be here. One bad apple spoils the bunch, and you are going to hinder growth, so you have to be taken out of the way.

“and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit. Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” That is the purging of Proverbs 16:6: iniquity purged, so we keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord and our God.

“Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.” We have to stay steadfast and abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures or our lust more than Christ, but doing the will of the Father and his Son.

precepts.text: The Lord knoweth them that are his, and he establishes leaders to guide you past the wiles of Satan. In a great house, Israel, there are vessels of gold and silver and also of wood and earth, some to honour and some to dishonour. Purge yourself from the wood and earth, the dead spirits always in some mess who separate from leadership and sit with the clique in the back, and you will be a vessel unto honour, meet for the master's use. You learned what the new moon was from a leadership video and now you avoid them?
precepts.point: The fear is not the fear of the servant who hid his talent or the brother making excuses because he is nervous; Psalms 119:120, my flesh trembleth for fear of thee and I am afraid of thy judgments. He is the King of terrors.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” The Lord already knows who are his; we do not, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so that you do not fall into the wiles of Satan or stumble into pitfalls and never recover.

“And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.” That is purging from sin, from the spiritual leaven, the same as “by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.”

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Just as not all the crops take root, in the house of Israel you have the good ones and the bad ones, some to honour and some to dishonour.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from the leaders the Lord established. How did you learn what the new moon was? You saw a video of our leadership teaching it. But then you come in here and do not want to be around them; you want to be with the clique in the back. That is the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

precepts.text: Partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption in the world through lust; add to your faith virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness, charity. Knowing that Christ is black is not enough; add to your repertoire. If these abound you shall not be barren nor unfruitful, and you will not be purged out. He that lacketh them is blind, cannot see afar off that America is destroyed and salvation is coming, and has forgotten he was purged from his old sins. Keep trimming or you end up back in the old folly.
precepts.point: The fear is not the fear of the servant who hid his talent or the brother making excuses because he is nervous; Psalms 119:120, my flesh trembleth for fear of thee and I am afraid of thy judgments. He is the King of terrors.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
“Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.” That escape from corruption is the purging of iniquity in Proverbs 16:6, and it has to be kept up.

“And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue.” We have to be diligent. We cannot just come in here knowing that Christ is black, God is black and the angels are black. When we come through these doors we have to add to our repertoire, add to our spirit: “virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity.”

“For if these things be in you, and abound”: not just be in you, but be in you and grow. “they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Meaning you do not have to be purged out. If you can do that, you do not have to worry about being taken out of the mix, because you are constantly growing and doing the Lord’s will.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind.” Sin has blinded you. You cannot think straight, you cannot do what is common sense, you struggle constantly and never break through, because you have not purged yourself from the wrong people and you love that pleasure more than God. He “cannot see afar off”: you cannot see that America is going to be destroyed and that salvation is coming. You are a situational Israelite living in the moment, thinking America is going to last forever. Shame.

He “hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” God purged you from your old sins, but if you do not keep trimming, if you do not keep purging, you will end up back in your old folly. This is a wake-up call, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness.

precepts.text: A just weight and balance are the Lord's; all the weights of the bag are his work. Deal justly and you are in the spirit.
precepts.point: The other side of the promise is that an unjust balance shortens your days. One day somebody realizes you have been robbing them, and men kill over a dollar. The Lord wrote that from the beginning.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“But thou shalt have a perfect and just weight, a perfect and just measure shalt thou have.” The Lord does not like people who are crooked. If you are going to do business, make sure you have a just balance; do not play with the scale and tilt it in your favor.

Solomon shows whose scale it is: “A just weight and balance are the Lord’s: all the weights of the bag are his work.” The just weight belongs to the Lord. So if you are dealing with a just weight and balance, you are in the spirit, and the Most High loves that.

The Most High is not a joke. He gives commandments on what you should do to live, and says keep them so that you may have life. Dealing justly with your brother is love, and “Owe no man any thing, but to love one another: for he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law.” Doing back-dealing with your brother shows no love; that is hatred. By being covetous you break many laws.

That is why the just weight comes with a promise: “that thy days may be lengthened in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.” The scale that is the Lord's is the scale that lengthens your days.

precepts.text: Let reason go before every enterprise, and counsel before every action. Apply the counsel and things go well.
precepts.point: Once a man has a little money he feels grown and asks who anyone is to counsel him. Months or years later, when everything falls apart, then he wants counsel. It is needed before, not after.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Why? Because of what you were supposed to do first: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Everything you take on to do, you are supposed to seek counsel. And if you seek counsel and apply it, things are going to go well for you.

But instead of seeking counsel, pride kicks in. I am my own man, I do what I want. A lot of times when brothers have bad dealings with each other, both of them were out of the spirit, because neither one ever asked for counsel: Listen, I want to do this job with so-and-so; what do you think about it?

Once people have a little money in their pocket, they feel grown. I own my own house, I bought it with my own money, I am doing better than you; who are you to counsel me? Then months later, years later, when everything falls apart, now they want counsel. Counsel did not go before that enterprise; pride went before it, and destruction came with it.

You need counsel before, not after. That is why we have to remember the scriptures: blessed is he that readeth, and if we apply what we read, we are going to be all right. Reason and counsel before every action is the cure for the pride that goes before destruction.

precepts.text: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the Lord weigheth the spirits. Everyone thinks they are righteous, but the Lord sees everything.
precepts.point: I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, to give every man according to his ways and the fruit of his doings. Most of us only see each other on the Sabbath on our best behaviour; six days a week nobody here knows what you are doing. The sister in Georgia bowed and said shalom for ten years while carrying on with the Uber Eats driver, and thought she was fooling the Most High.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

precepts.why:
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?” The heart is the mind, and nothing is more deceitful than the mind. Christ showed what comes out of it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”

Yet Solomon says, “All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes”. Every one of us thinks we are righteous. Ask them: me? I ain't do nothing. Covetous spirit? Hatred? Oh, no. Judas would have said the same. All our ways are clean in our own eyes.

“but the Lord weigheth the spirits.” The Lord sees everything, and you cannot hide from the Most High. You can fool the deacon, you can fool the bishop and the leadership, but the Most High sees you, and you are not fooling yourself either. You know where you were last night, why you never called the brother back, and why you told her to hush before you answered the phone.

That is Jeremiah 17:10: “I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins”. Only God can search the mind, and he weighs what is really in it, not what we show each other. Read on: “Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established.”

precepts.text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
precepts.point: Especially those who know the scriptures and choose not to obey them: that is a proud look.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

precepts.text: A man with no rule over his own spirit is a city broken down and without walls — every provocation walks straight in.
precepts.point: In the red rage you are blinded. Everybody knows where your buttons are; a man disciplined in the spirit controls that. Rule your spirit and you will conquer cities.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: That one verse explains it all: when you are angry nothing godlike is coming out of you. This is the carnal wrath of a man, not the righteous indignation we rebuke with in the streets.
precepts.point: In the red rage you are blinded. Everybody knows where your buttons are; a man disciplined in the spirit controls that. Rule your spirit and you will conquer cities.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: Anger resting in the bosom of fools means it is always ready to pop out. You wear it on your chest and that is your default, and it is a childish reaction.
precepts.point: In the red rage you are blinded. Everybody knows where your buttons are; a man disciplined in the spirit controls that. Rule your spirit and you will conquer cities.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

precepts.text: When a man's ways please the Lord, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him; that is what happened with Esau.
precepts.point: The same prayer belongs to us: pray for all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness, keeping the commandments until Christ returns.

note.label: Genesis 33: The Meeting With Esau

precepts.why:
“When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” That is what happened with Esau.

Jacob bowed himself to the ground seven times as he came near, and Esau “ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.” That embrace is not proof that the hatred was gone. Jacob had prayed for deliverance, and the Most High put that peace on Esau in that moment, because Jacob's ways pleased Him.

precepts.text: The lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord; the Lord decided the outcome of the inheritance of these lands.
precepts.point: The description of the seven parts was to be brought to Joshua, that he may cast lots for them before the Lord. Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
Joshua says to describe the land into seven parts and bring it to him, “that I may cast lots for you here before the Lord our God.” Casting lots is like throwing dice or drawing straws: you may be the one throwing, but the Lord decides what comes up. “The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord.”

So the inheritance of these lands was not Joshua's choosing. The lot was cast before the Lord, and the Lord decided the outcome of who received what.

precepts.text: Pride goeth before destruction; the brother became prideful and high, and it brought him to a fall.
precepts.point: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” The brother became prideful and high, and it brought him to a fall.

“But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction”. Uzziah went into the temple to burn incense upon the altar of incense, which was not his office. When the priests withstood him, “Uzziah was wroth”, and while he was wroth, with a censer in his hand, “the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests”. He “was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house”, “cut off from the house of the Lord”.

The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is.

precepts.text: When a man's ways please the Most High he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.
precepts.point: Sisters forced to wear pants at work should keep a skirt or dress in the car or book bag, change in the bathroom on the way out if they can, and ask the Most High for mercy; these are things done in captivity.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“the shields of the earth belong unto God: he is greatly exalted.” Because he reigns over the heathen, “When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.”

The favor to have the Sabbath off, the new moon off, the feast days, to wear fringes and to have the head wrapped at work is only of the Most High, who rules over the Gentile nations. When our ways please him, he makes even our enemies be at peace with us. Sisters forced to wear pants at work should keep a skirt or dress in the car or book bag, change in the bathroom on the way out if they can, and ask the Most High for mercy; these are things done in captivity, and the favor comes from him.

precepts.text: When a man's ways please the Most High, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him; Daniel was operating in a righteous spirit.
precepts.point: The king was glad and commanded Daniel taken up, and no manner of hurt was found on him because he believed in his God; then the accusers, their children, and wives were cast in and the lions brake their bones before they reached the bottom.

note.label: Daniel 6: Daniel in the Den of Lions

precepts.why:
“When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” Daniel's ways pleased the Lord, and so even the lions were at peace with him: “My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me”. Daniel was operating in a righteous spirit, innocent before God, and “before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.”

The king was exceeding glad and commanded Daniel taken up out of the den, and “no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.” The same lions that were at peace with Daniel had the mastery of his accusers, their children, and their wives, and brake all their bones in pieces before they came to the bottom of the den. The difference was not the lions; it was whose ways pleased the Lord.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness”. The Most High took the children of Israel down because of sin and rebellion. “I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee.” We didn't want to keep the law.

“Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities”. God destroyed us because of sin. “therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee”. You don't want his laws? Okay, I've got something for you. I'm going to give you to whatever you want. “and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee.” That's how we fell as a nation.

note.label: The Building Blocks of Bitterness

points: Commit thy works unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shall be established. So as your thoughts or your intentions are discerned by the word of God, God says I will establish your thought process, I will establish your intentions according to the word of God. If you are not living a double life, but you are committing your works unto the Lord, the Bible says he will establish your thoughts. That bitterness that is brewing within us, that bitterness that is stirring up, that hatred, the Lord will establish all of that if you commit yourself to the works.

But then you join yourself and you say, we sick boss, our house on fire boss. You associate yourselves with him. The Bible says he shall not be unpunished. He is still going to get it. And so are you.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

points: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city. In the household you have to be slow to anger and deal with your wife as the weaker vessel. You figure out how to control your spirit at camp when a man twice your size is standing in front of you; control it at home too.

Now, if you have a wife that is unruly, stand up for yourself. But if you have a sister that does what she is supposed to do for the most part, there has to be a balance. Your wife cannot always see the worst part of you.

note.label: This Woman's Work

points: Pride. Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. You think you know it all, you think you have all the wisdom and understanding; but pride is the progenitor of your destruction, because pride removes correction. You do not want to hear it. Pride isolates you, and pride precedes the collapse.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

points: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord: though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished. You think you can hold hands with the wicked and not get touched. Some of you will defend the wicked and make excuses for them: a prideful spouse, a wicked child. When God brings the judgment, if you are joining hands trying to protect them, it reaches you too.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged, and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil. Christ strengthens you to resist sin; that is why we remove the leaven, which represents sin. Purge means to free from moral defilement and to cause evacuation: get the leaven out of the house, put the blood on the doorpost, and be delivered from your captors.

The fear is not the fear of the servant who hid his talent or the brother making excuses because he is nervous; Psalms 119:120, my flesh trembleth for fear of thee and I am afraid of thy judgments. He is the King of terrors.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

points: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. Bad dealings usually mean both brothers were out of the spirit, because neither asked for counsel first.
Once a man has a little money he feels grown and asks who anyone is to counsel him. Months or years later, when everything falls apart, then he wants counsel. It is needed before, not after.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil. Strait means narrow and difficult, not merely straight.
Everyone will fall and make mistakes on the way; the point is to keep walking.

note.label: The Highway of the Upright: an Israelites's Strait Journey

points: That is what happened to that brother: the haughty spirit came before his fall.
A man who sins against himself is the destroyer of his own soul.
It is about him and not about the people. The people in there are worshipping him.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: It seems right to go and do it, and the end of it is death.
We can't use good intents to do evil works or to cover up foolishness.
Learn how to follow orders in his truth and follow what the Most High set before us.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Authority exposes your character the way money does. Most men never had authority before marriage — never led a home, a woman, a child or a family budget.

An insecure man becomes controlling down to the colour of the grout. An angry man becomes harsh, an immature man inconsistent, a lazy man negligent, a prideful man a tyrant. A wise man becomes a foundation; a man who fears God becomes a shepherd to his household.
Authority exposes the man, not the wife. That is why you cannot say it is the woman you were given.
In the red rage you are blinded. Everybody knows where your buttons are; a man disciplined in the spirit controls that. Rule your spirit and you will conquer cities.

note.label: To Whom Much Is Given: The Burden and Beauty of Godly Leadership

points: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” We fell because of sin and rebellion. We're the ones who have to change this and stop it. We've only started; there's a lot of work to do.
